citation.title: Chapter 2: Plasma confinement and transport
citation.authors: ITER Physics Expert Group on Confinement and Transport; ITER Physics Expert Group on Confinement Modelling and Database; ITER Physics Basis Editors
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown (no DOI for this chapter appears in the supplied text)

topic: ITER Physics Basis review of tokamak confinement and transport: H-mode, edge pedestal, transport barriers, confinement scalings, transport modelling, and particle and momentum transport
own_question: How can ITER confinement be projected from present experiments, and how uncertain are those projections?
actual_method_and_evidence: A review chapter that synthesizes multi-machine databases, global regression scalings, dimensionless similarity experiments and 1D transport model tests. It contains no CES nowcasting, no BES/ECEI estimator work, no KSTAR data and no analysis of real-time timing.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The H-mode is defined by a narrow edge transport barrier (pedestal), and pedestal parameters are linked to overall confinement in the multi-machine data reviewed.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a review of DIII-D, ASDEX-Upgrade and JET results. Pedestal width scalings vary between machines. The pedestal quantities discussed are mostly electron quantities and are not CES impurity Ti.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. The chapter mentions that rotation is measured with charge-exchange impurity emission, but it says nothing about report cadence or arrival times.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable to our study. The uncertainty intervals given in the chapter apply to confinement-time regression.
forbidden_inferences: That this source supports BES/ECEI-to-CES inference or nowcasting
That impurity CES Ti equals main-ion Ti
That any KSTAR pedestal behaviour follows from it
That the chapter shows real-time feasibility
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Use it optionally as a general background citation for the H-mode pedestal and transport barrier. It provides no evidence on the paper's methods or targets.
